title: Employee Hierarchy Depth
description:
For every employee, compute their **depth in the org hierarchy** (CEO = depth 0) and the **total number of direct and indirect reports** under them (leaf nodes count as 0).

**Table: employees** — `id`, `name`, `salary`, `manager_id`

Output columns: `name`, `depth`, `total_reports`. Order by `depth`, `name`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, salary INT, manager_id INT); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Ada',200000,NULL),(2,'Ben',150000,1),(3,'Cara',90000,2),(4,'Drew',80000,2),(5,'Eve',120000,1),(6,'Fay',70000,5),(7,'Gil',65000,3);
solution_sql: WITH RECURSIVE depth_cte AS (SELECT id, name, 0 AS depth FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT e.id, e.name, d.depth + 1 FROM employees e JOIN depth_cte d ON e.manager_id = d.id), subtree AS (SELECT id AS root_id, id AS member_id FROM employees UNION ALL SELECT s.root_id, e.id FROM subtree s JOIN employees e ON e.manager_id = s.member_id) SELECT d.name, d.depth, COUNT(s.member_id) - 1 AS total_reports FROM depth_cte d JOIN subtree s ON d.id = s.root_id GROUP BY d.id, d.name, d.depth ORDER BY d.depth, d.name

test_cases.description: Ada depth 0 reports 6; Ben depth 1 reports 3; Eve depth 1 reports 1; Cara depth 2 reports 1; Drew+Fay depth 2 reports 0; Gil depth 3 reports 0

hints: Use one recursive CTE for depth (top-down traversal from root).
Use another recursive CTE for subtree membership (to count all descendants per node).
total_reports = count of subtree members - 1 (excluding self).
explanation: Recursive CTE `depth_cte` assigns depths top-down. Recursive CTE `subtree` expands each node to all its descendants (including itself). Joining them and counting descendants (minus self) gives total_reports. Ada (root) has 6 reports under her. Ben has 3 (Cara, Drew, Gil). Eve has 1 (Fay). Cara has 1 (Gil). Drew, Fay, Gil are leaf nodes with 0 reports.
